claims.knowledge: Fifth syllabus topic is Principles of Electromechanical Energy Conversion
claims.scope: The syllabus lists Chapter 5 separately. No standalone Chapter 5 lecture file was supplied. Pages 3–13 of the DC lecture provide the core material; its hardware and machine topics from page 14 onward are organized as Chapter 6.

claims.knowledge: Motional EMF, conductor force and directions; ei=Fv
claims.scope: DC lecture pages 4–6. The scalar expressions assume a perpendicular, uniform field and the terminal, current and velocity references displayed in the diagram.

claims.knowledge: Linear machine KVL, motor/generator modes, unloaded ideal speed
claims.scope: DC lecture pages 6–10. The source changes its current arrow for generator operation; this chapter keeps one signed current reference throughout.

claims.knowledge: Coupled KVL/Newton dynamics and energy balance
claims.scope: Derived extension of DC lecture page 6 with finite inductance and viscous drag. Parameters are illustrative. RK4 evaluates the differential equations; the curves are not measurements.

claims.knowledge: Speed units, Newton rotation, work/power and uniform-field coil
claims.scope: DC lecture pages 11–12 provide rotational mechanics. The uniform-field loop is a separately verified extension, using a generated-EMF convention and an explicitly defined positive area normal.

claims.knowledge: Original active-conductor geometry and loop exercise
claims.scope: DC lecture page 13 was visually inspected. Radius, radial field and end-region assumptions are disclosed in the worked example. They are modeling conditions, not inferred measurements.

claims.knowledge: Energy/coenergy derivatives and linear overlap actuator
claims.scope: MIT Chapter 8, pages 2–5, supplies the energy/coenergy method. The original illustrative actuator geometry is evaluated with a linear reluctance model. No force dataset is claimed.
DC lecture page 7 and the MIT energy-conversion treatment. Power is balanced across a consistently defined electrical, mechanical and storage boundary.

models.title: Conductor force and motional EMF
models.parameters: Active length 0.50 m; adjustable signed B, i and v.
models.assumptions: Uniform perpendicular field. Positive B is into the page, positive i down the bar and positive v to the right.
models.checks: At the initial settings: e = 3.2 V, F = 1.2 N and ei = Fv = 9.6 W.

models.title: Static linear DC machine
models.parameters: Supply 12 V; R = 2 ohm; k = 0.4 in SI units.
models.assumptions: Externally imposed velocity. Negligible inductive voltage and friction. The source can absorb regenerated power.
models.checks: At v = 20 m/s: input 24 W, conversion 16 W, heat 8 W. At 45 m/s: input −36 W, conversion −54 W, heat 18 W.

models.title: Dynamic linear DC machine
models.assumptions: Initial current and speed are zero. Parameters are constant. Fourth-order Runge–Kutta uses a 0.002 s step.
models.checks: Steady speed is 24 m/s and current is 1.2 A. Independent audit compares the trajectory with the closed-form two-state solution and checks instantaneous energy balance.

models.title: Uniform-field rotating coil
models.parameters: N = 40 turns; A = 0.02 m²; B = 0.5 T; angular speed 10 rad/s.
models.assumptions: Positive current follows the positive area normal by the right-hand rule. Positive angular speed increases theta. No commutator is present.
models.checks: Torque × angular speed + generated EMF × current = 0. EMF is zero at 0 degrees and has a 4 V peak at 90 degrees.

models.title: Two active conductors in a radial gap
models.parameters: B = 1 T; active length 1 m; radius 0.5 m; current magnitude 1 A.
models.assumptions: Both active sides are under opposite pole faces at the displayed instant. End conductors lie outside the active field.
models.checks: At 6.28 rad/s: total EMF magnitude 6.28 V, torque magnitude 1 N m and speed 59.9696 rpm.

models.title: Linear coenergy overlap actuator
models.parameters: N = 200 turns; depth 0.02 m; overlap 0.01–0.08 m; each gap 0.001–0.005 m.
models.assumptions: Two equal air gaps, infinite core permeability, and negligible fringing, leakage and saturation. Position is imposed.
models.checks: At x = 0.04 m, g = 0.002 m and i = 2 A: L = 0.01005309649 H and F = 0.5026548246 N. Force also matches the finite difference of coenergy at constant current.

examples.title: Moving conductor
examples.given: B = 0.8 T, length 0.5 m, speed 8 m/s, current 3 A.
examples.result: EMF 3.2 V; force 1.2 N; converted power 9.6 W.

examples.title: Motor and generator operation
examples.given: Supply 12 V, R = 2 ohm, k = 0.4; speeds 20 and 45 m/s.
examples.result: At 20 m/s: current 2 A, converted power 16 W. At 45 m/s: current −3 A, converted power −54 W.
examples.verification: Electrical input − copper loss − mechanical conversion = 0.

examples.title: Steady operating point after a linear start
examples.result: Speed 24 m/s; current 1.2 A; input 14.4 W = copper loss 2.88 W + drag loss 11.52 W.
examples.source: Derived from L05 page 6 and the MIT8 energy balance.
examples.verification: KVL and force balance agree. Initial current remains zero with finite inductance.

examples.title: Original rotating-loop exercise
examples.given: Angular speed 6.28 rad/s; current 1 A; B = 1 T; three specified sides each 1 m.
examples.result: Mechanical frequency 0.999493043 Hz; speed 59.96958256 rpm; two 1 N forces; 1 N m torque magnitude; 6.28 V total EMF magnitude.
examples.verification: Conditional on radius 0.5 m and the radial-gap model. Torque and EMF are calculated independently from conductor laws. Reversing current does not change prescribed-motion EMF.

examples.title: Coenergy actuator
examples.given: N = 200, depth 0.02 m, overlap 0.04 m, each gap 0.002 m, current 2 A.
examples.source: Derived from MIT8 and the linear magnetic reluctance relation.
examples.verification: Finite difference of coenergy with overlap at fixed current agrees with the analytic force.

errata.issue: The ideal no-load speed V/(B length) can be mistaken for a loaded operating point.
errata.correction: It assumes zero opposing mechanical load and friction. The dynamic laboratory separately includes viscous drag.

errata.issue: The generator equation switches to a positive outgoing-current reference.
errata.correction: A single signed current reference is retained; generator operation has negative current.

errata.issue: Work = torque × angle is shown without a constant-torque condition.
errata.correction: General work is the integral of torque with angle. The product applies for constant torque.

errata.issue: Radius and the end-field approximation are implicit, and terminal signs need defined references.
errata.correction: State the 1 m span as a diameter, the ideal radial-gap field and inactive end conductors. Maintain the prescribed rotation when discussing current reversal.

errata.issue: Inductance is omitted, so the immediate current V/R is idealized.
errata.correction: Keep the zero-inductance case as a static approximation. With finite L, initial current is continuous and its initial derivative is V/L.
